bottleneck.description: Category-creator and leader in cube/grid ASRS with ~1,900 installations and a global integrator channel, but the same retrieval workload can be served by competing ASRS architectures (shuttles, mini-loads, robot AMR-to-rack) from many vendors.

dependency.key_customers: Puma, Best Buy, Asda, Lidl, Gucci, H Mart, Siemens, plus white-label deployments through Dematic, Swisslog, Bastian, KNAPP and Element Logic
dependency.key_suppliers: Aluminium grid extruders, lithium battery suppliers, wheel/motor vendors, IPC/PLC controllers, integrators provide site engineering

editorial.notes: AutoStore is the clear leader inside the narrow cube-storage sub-segment and the Ocado settlement gives both parties cross-licensed access to pre-2020 patents, so the legal moat has weakened. Outside the cube niche, customers can substitute Exotec Skypod, Geek+, Hai Robotics, AutoStore-style clones (Element Logic uses AutoStore but BMG and others build alternatives), shuttle ASRS from Dematic/SSI Schaefer/TGW, or traditional mini-loads — all competitive on $/throughput. The technology advantage is real but not a sole-source position. Aligns with the SYM LOW anchor (warehouse automation, contested).
